item.title: Where can battery-run rickshaws operate under new rules?
item.description:
Battery-run rickshaws will be barred from national highways, expressways, elevated expressways and Bus Rapid Transit (BRT) roads under new regulations issued by the government to regulate their movement and restore order on city streets.
The Local Government Division under the Ministry of Local Government, Rural Development and Cooperatives issued the regulations through a notification on Thursday.
Titled City Corporation Areas Three-Wheeled Low-Speed Battery-Run Rickshaw Movement Regulations, 2026, the rules will apply to battery-run rickshaws operating in all city corporation areas across the country.
Under the regulations, the relevant authorities and traffic departments will jointly designate routes by zone. Rickshaws operating in one zone will not be allowed to enter another, and drivers must keep to the left lane.
The rules also prohibit horns exceeding 40 decibels. In areas near schools, hospitals, places of worship and other crowded locations, the maximum permitted speed will be 15km per hour.
Driving on footpaths, using mobile phones while driving, and unauthorised overtaking or lane changes will be prohibited.
Rickshaws will also be restricted in the number of passengers and the goods they can carry. They may carry either two or four passengers, in addition to the driver, while commercial goods other than passengers’ hand-carried belongings will not be allowed.
The regulations also set out requirements for battery charging and disposal. Batteries may only be charged at authorised charging points or garages. Authorities will gradually move to make net metering, solar panels and renewable energy mandatory at charging stations.
Discarded or non-functional batteries must not be dumped in open spaces, on the ground or in water bodies, or burned. Battery sellers will be required to take back an old battery whenever they sell a new one.

item.title: A final call for help, then a death under suspicion
item.description:
A desperate video call to her father, a plea to be rescued from alleged abuse and an abrupt disconnection were among the last known moments of 24-year-old Jumratun Nessa Barsha, whose death at her husband’s home in Dhaka has prompted a murder investigation.
Barsha had called her family around midnight on Tuesday, crying and asking to be taken home, according to her relatives. She reportedly feared she would be killed if she remained there.
When her parents rushed to the house in Monipuripara, they found an ambulance waiting outside. Her in-laws told them she had died by suicide.
At Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, the family learned that Barsha was dead.
Police have since arrested her husband, Nabid Hossain, following a complaint filed by her father, Sheikh Monowar Hossain.
Tejgaon police station Officer-in-Charge Muniruzzaman told Dhaka Tribune on Thursday that Barsha had allegedly been subjected to repeated assaults over dowry demands.
Injury marks were found on her body, he said.
Nabid was arrested at the hospital and produced before a court. The investigation is continuing.
The family disputes the account of suicide given by Barsha’s in-laws and alleges that she was killed following prolonged abuse.
Police have not yet established the cause of death.
Barsha and Nabid married about a year ago after a relationship.
According to her father, trouble began after the marriage when Nabid repeatedly demanded money from his wife’s family.
He alleged that Nabid, who was unemployed, sought financial assistance on several occasions. The family initially gave him money, but the demands continued, frequently leading to arguments and physical abuse.
Relatives said Nabid had also sought money to start a business and buy a motorcycle.
On Tuesday night, Barsha was allegedly assaulted again.
Her family said someone from her in-laws’ household recorded part of the incident and sent the footage to them. The contents and authenticity of the recording have not been independently established.
Around midnight, Barsha contacted her parents through a video call.
She was crying, describing the alleged abuse and asking them to take her away, her family said.
The call suddenly ended.
Alarmed, her parents left for Monipuripara, reaching the house at approximately 12:30am.
An ambulance was parked outside.
According to the family, Barsha’s in-laws claimed she had taken her own life and was being taken to hospital.
Her parents followed the ambulance to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital, where they learned of her death.
The discovery of injuries on Barsha’s body has added to questions surrounding the circumstances of her death.
Her father’s complaint alleges that she was killed following repeated dowry-related abuse.
Police have arrested Nabid, but the allegations against him have not been proved in court.
Investigators must now establish what happened after Barsha’s final video call, examine the reported footage and determine whether the physical evidence supports the family’s allegations or the account given by her in-laws.
No statement from Nabid or his family responding to the allegations was available in the reports reviewed.
For Barsha’s parents, the unanswered questions begin with the call they received that night, when their daughter asked them to bring her home, but they could not reach her in time.

item.title: The controversy behind the attention on Tahsif Souri’s death
item.description:
The discovery of former Bangladesh Air Force flight lieutenant KM Tahsif Souri’s body in Dhaka’s Turag River has drawn widespread attention, not only because of the unexplained circumstances surrounding his death but also because of his name’s earlier association with a controversial video of Sheikh Hasina leaving Bangladesh during the August 2024 mass uprising.
Tahsif, 28, was found dead on Wednesday, a day after leaving his Uttara home to meet a younger acquaintance. His father has alleged murder, while police have yet to establish the cause of death.
The former officer had previously been named in media reports alleging that he was involved in recording or circulating footage of the then-prime minister’s departure from the country on August 5, 2024.
He had questioned those allegations, while the Inter-Services Public Relations Directorate (ISPR) rejected separate claims that his departure from the Air Force was linked to a foreign intelligence agency.
The controversy has resurfaced following his death, prompting renewed public discussion about his military career and the circumstances in which he left the service.
However, investigators have not established any connection between those earlier events and his death.
Tahsif first drew public attention following allegations that he was involved in recording or circulating footage of Sheikh Hasina leaving Bangladesh as her government collapsed amid the mass uprising on August 5, 2024.
The video circulated widely on social media, prompting questions about who had recorded and released it.
A subsequent media report identified Tahsif and another Air Force officer, Flight Lieutenant Rifat Ashrafi, in connection with the controversy.
The report also alleged that the two officers had been forced into retirement because of suspected links with a foreign intelligence agency.
However, ISPR rejected that allegation in a statement issued on August 4, 2025.
It said the two officers had been retired through due process under the Air Force’s existing laws and regulations in a different context.
Tahsif himself questioned the claims about the video.
In an interview published on a YouTube channel earlier this year, he challenged those making the allegation to provide evidence that he had recorded or circulated the footage.
He also suggested that the controversy might have contributed to his departure from the Air Force, although he did not establish that as a fact.
Tahsif’s father said the family had been informed that his son was removed from the Air Force over disciplinary issues in September 2024.
Following his departure, Tahsif worked with several organisations, including the Bangladesh Cricket Board and Netra News, according to his family.
Relatives and former colleagues said the loss of his position had affected him deeply.
A former colleague told BBC Bangla that Tahsif had accumulated around 200 hours of flying experience and considered becoming a pilot his dream career.
The colleague also said Tahsif faced social pressure following allegations published about him.
His father said Tahsif occasionally expressed apprehension but had not disclosed any specific threat.
These accounts provide background to the public interest surrounding his death, but they do not establish how or why he died.
The case now centres on several unanswered questions: whom Tahsif met after leaving home, where he went that night, what happened after his final message and how his body ended up in the Turag.
His father’s allegation of murder remains unproven, while the initial inquest does not establish a definitive cause of death.
The controversy surrounding his Air Force career has made the case unusually prominent, but any suggestion that it motivated his death would be premature without supporting evidence.
For now, the public attention surrounding Tahsif Souri’s death reflects both the unanswered circumstances of his final hours and the unresolved questions about a controversial chapter of his past.

item.title: NCP to demonstrate at Shahbagh on Friday, calling on at least 3 ministers to resign
item.description:
The National Citizen Party (NCP) has called a mass protest at Shahbagh on Friday, pressing a five-point charter of demands led by the resignation of Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed and Energy Minister Iqbal Hassan Mahmood.
In a message issued Thursday night, the party said it was demanding the two ministers step down for failing to ensure public safety and energy security.
Among the other demands, the NCP called for dissolving the "one-party-dominated" committee on constitutional amendment and forming a constitutional reform council in line with the referendum verdict.
The party also demanded the repeal of all laws that run counter to human rights and freedom of expression, and insisted that the proposed amendments to the Cyber Security Act must not be passed.
It further called for completing the trials over the July mass killings and implementing the verdicts without delay, and for the removal of the Inspector General of Police (IGP) over what it termed questionable remarks on extrajudicial killings.
Speaking to UNB, NCP Joint Convener Sarwar Tusher said party leaders and other members of its political council would gather at Shahbagh for the protest over the five demands.
"This should not be called a grand rally," he said, adding that the program would begin in Dhaka and be followed by similar protests in divisional cities in phases.
He said the party plans to hold a large-scale rally after the protest programs conclude.

item.title: Therapy centre offers new hope to people with disabilities in Gaibandha
item.description:
A specialised therapy centre in Gaibandha is helping people with disabilities regain mobility and improve their quality of life, bringing rehabilitation services closer to underserved communities in the northern district.
The Friendship Therapy Centre, established in 2023, provides rehabilitation support to children and adults with physical and neurological disabilities, including those who have difficulty moving their limbs or carrying out everyday activities.
The initiative, run by development organisation Friendship, has enabled several patients to regain movement and perform daily activities with greater independence, according to rehabilitation officials and beneficiaries.
Among them is 45-year-old Raja Mia, a resident of Char Ratanpur, whose life changed following an accident four years ago.
“After the accident, I could not move properly. But after receiving services from the therapy centre, I can now walk and move around. I am doing reasonably well,” he said.
His wife described the difficulties the family faced before he began receiving rehabilitation services.
“He used to remain bedridden and could not move his arms or legs. We have been receiving treatment from the Friendship Therapy Centre for the past two years. Now he can move around,” she said.
However, she said her husband still requires advanced medical treatment to make further progress in his recovery.
Farhana Ashrekin, rehabilitation officer at the Friendship Therapy Centre in Gaibandha, said the organisation launched its rehabilitation program in 2020, while the dedicated therapy centre began operations in 2023.
“Since then, we have been providing therapy services to children and adults with neurological impairments and difficulties moving their arms and legs,” she said.
She said regular therapy had helped many patients improve muscle movement and functional mobility.
“Some patients who previously remained bedridden are now able to sit up, while others have gradually regained the ability to stand and walk,” she added.
The program is particularly significant for people living in remote char areas, where access to specialised healthcare and rehabilitation services remains limited.
Matiar Rahman, chairman of Kamarjani Union Parishad under Gaibandha Sadar upazila, said Friendship’s activities had improved access to services and assistance for people with disabilities in the area.
He said the organisation had distributed wheelchairs and recreational materials while working closely with the union parishad to identify people requiring support.
“Friendship’s work for people with disabilities in our union is commendable. We are working together to ensure they receive the assistance they need,” he said.
According to the chairman, approximately 350 people with disabilities live in Kamarjani union.
He said coordination with Friendship had made it easier for local authorities to identify eligible beneficiaries and facilitate access to government disability allowances.
The organisation has also supported an educational initiative called Baranda School in Koraibari, providing learning opportunities for children with disabilities.
Rahman called for the establishment of a dedicated school for children with disabilities in the union.
“My dream is to establish a model school for children with disabilities in Kamarjani,” he said.
He also urged the authorities to introduce larger, specially equipped boats to ensure safer transportation and evacuation for people with disabilities during floods, a recurring challenge in the riverine region.
Barrister Ayesha Taasin Khan, senior director and head of Inclusive Citizenship at Friendship, said the therapy centre had helped change attitudes towards disability within families.
She said parents and other family members were becoming more optimistic as they witnessed improvements in the physical abilities and daily functioning of children receiving rehabilitation support.
“The way we are caring for and giving importance to children with disabilities is creating greater hope among their family members,” she said.
Khan said the initiative had originally been designed to serve residents of remote char communities, but demand had expanded beyond those areas.
“We initially planned to provide services only to char residents. However, people from the mainland are also coming to the therapy centre for treatment,” she said.
Describing the growing demand as a significant development, she expressed hope that similar centres could be established in other underserved areas with government support.
She said expanding rehabilitation facilities would help more people with disabilities access essential services closer to their homes.

item.title: NBR: 10-30 count cotton yarn refers to single count yarn
item.description:
The National Board of Revenue (NBR) has issued a clarification regarding the order concerning the withdrawal of bond facilities and the provision for importing 10–30 count cotton yarn against bank guarantees.
According to an order issued on Thursday (29 October), the "10–30 count cotton yarn" mentioned in two previous directives specifically refers to 10–30 single count cotton yarn.
Signed by NBR Second Secretary (Customs: Export and Bond) Kazi Raihanuzzaman, the order noted that on 7 September, the bond facility for importing 10–30 count cotton yarn was withdrawn to protect local industry interests and streamline raw material access for genuine exporters.
Under that rule, genuine exporters holding warehouse licenses were permitted to import against bank guarantees. The order was subsequently amended on 8 October.
The directive further stated that these measures were adopted in line with decisions made at the first meeting of an inter-ministerial committee formed to review and resolve existing issues in the textile sector.
Issued under the powers conferred by Section 266 of the Customs Act, 2023, the order takes effect immediately.

item.title: Bata Bangladesh reports 189% EPS growth in Q3 2026
item.description:
Bata Bangladesh, a leading footwear brand, reported year-on-year turnover growth of 15% in the third quarter of 2026 (July–September), with YTD growth 11%, reflecting the resilience of its core business amid challenging global and domestic economic conditions.
The company recorded quarterly turnover of Tk211 crore with Tk779.8 crore in YTD.
Persistent inflation continued to constrain household spending, while geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and other global uncertainties pushed up energy, production, logistics, and raw material costs.
From January to September 2026, company had a total profit of TK45.4 crore after tax, with earnings per share (EPS) rose to Tk33.2, which is 256% growth from the same period last year.
The company remains focused on sustaining its business momentum through new product introductions, expansion into new retail locations, retail transformation and stronger omnichannel integration.
Bata is also strengthening its digital and e-commerce platforms to make shopping more convenient and accessible for customers nationwide.
Ongoing initiatives to improve cost efficiency and optimize sourcing are expected to support further gains in profitability by the end of 2026.
Commenting on the results, Faria Yasmin, managing director of Bata Bangladesh, said: “Despite global geopolitical tensions and persistent inflationary pressures, Bata Bangladesh has maintained its business momentum and delivered encouraging turnover growth till Q3. Our continued focus on expanding our retail presence, introducing new products that combine comfort and style, and engaging younger and fashion-conscious consumers remains central to our growth strategy. We are also committed to enhancing the customer experience through our digital platforms and omnichannel initiatives.”
Demonstrating its commitment to shareholder returns, Bata Bangladesh also declared an interim cash dividend of 36.3%.
With a continued focus on customer-centric innovation, retail expansion, digital transformation and operational efficiency, Bata Bangladesh aims to strengthen its market position and build sustainable growth for the remainder of 2026.

item.title: TikTok releases Q2 2026 community guidelines enforcement report
item.description:
TikTok on Thursday released its Q2 2026 Community Guidelines Enforcement Report, highlighting the platform’s ongoing commitment to creating a safe digital space for its users.
The report covers data from April to June 2026 and details the proactive steps TikTok has taken to identify and remove content that violates its Community Guidelines.
These measures aim to ensure a positive experience for its global community.
In Q2 2026, TikTok removed a total of 14,791,485 videos in Bangladesh for violating its Community Guidelines.
This represented approximately 0.9% of all content uploaded to the platform.
TikTok proactively identified and removed 99.8% of these videos before users reported them.
Of the proactively removed videos, 92.7% were taken down within 24 hours of posting, and a total of 205,001 videos were later restored to the platform.
Globally, TikTok removed 188 million (188,298,141) videos, equivalent to approximately 0.5% of all content uploaded to the platform.
Of these, 183,344,707 videos were removed through automated detection technologies.
The global proactive removal rate stood at 99.5%, with 92.7% of videos removed within 24 hours. A total of 6,262,383 videos were reinstated after review.
During Q2 2026, TikTok’s AI systems became increasingly effective at identifying and removing older content.
TikTok also removed comments that violated its policies on potentially offensive or inappropriate content.
Globally, a total of 278,384,463 comments were removed in Q2 2026, up from 237,517,128 in Q1 2026.
The platform also removed 146,807,400 fake accounts during the quarter.
An additional 26,840,767 accounts suspected of belonging to users under the age of 13 were removed to help protect younger users.
The report provides further details on the types of content removed for violating TikTok’s policies. Sensitive or mature themes accounted for 19.5% of removed videos.
Another 13.7% violated the platform’s safety and civility standards. Of the removed videos, 13.5% were identified as containing dangerous activities and challenges, and 13.8% involved body exposure and sexualized behaviors.
Meanwhile, 1.8% of the videos removed were flagged as edited media and AI-generated content (AIGC).
The periodic publication of the Community Guidelines Enforcement Report offers insights into the scale and nature of content and account actions, underscoring TikTok's commitment to full transparency.
For detailed insights into the Q2 202 6 report and to learn more about TikTok's content guidelines, tools, and policies, visit TikTok's Transparency Centre, available in Bangla and English .

item.title: Three fires in nine days leave 12 burned in Gazipur
item.description:
Twelve people, including children, have suffered burns in three separate fire incidents in Gazipur over the past nine days, raising concerns over gas leaks and fire safety in residential areas.
All the injured are receiving treatment at the National Institute of Burn and Plastic Surgery in Dhaka, the institute’s resident surgeon Dr Sultan Mahmud Sikder confirmed.
In the first incident, three members of the same family suffered severe burns in a gas leak explosion in the Cherag Ali Market area of Tongi around 6:00am on October 21.
According to hospital sources, 85% to 95% of their bodies were burned. All three remain in critical condition, with two receiving treatment in the emergency department and the third in the High Dependency Unit (HDU).
On October 23, four members of another family suffered burns in a fire at their home in Gazipur.
Preliminary information suggests the fire started on a sofa early that morning before spreading to the wooden ceiling, two motorcycles parked on the balcony and eventually the entire house. The exact cause of the fire remains unknown. The injured were initially taken to Shaheed Tajuddin Ahmad Medical College Hospital before being transferred to the burn institute for advanced treatment.
Of the four, the mother and elder son have been admitted, while the father and younger son are under observation. The injured include two children aged four and five. One sustained burns to 40% of his body, while the other two family members suffered burns to 2% and 12% of their bodies, respectively.
In the latest incident, five members of the same family were burned in a fire caused by a gas leak in the Sardagong area of Kashimpur, Gazipur, around 8:30am on Thursday. They were brought to the burn institute in Dhaka around 2:00pm.
The family’s head, 40-year-old Riazul Sheikh, suffered burns to around 40% of his body and is in critical condition.
Arifa Begum suffered burns to 5% of her body, while 17-year-old Faria sustained burns to 8%. Eighteen-year-old Rozina and one-year-old Mohammad Rahim each suffered burns to less than 1% of their bodies.
All five are receiving treatment and remain under medical observation.
